title: Exhaust Valve Control Solenoid Circuit High (Bank 1)
plain: The exhaust valve control solenoid on bank 1 is an electric valve that adjusts valve timing or lift using oil pressure. The computer found a voltage that is too high in its circuit.

causes.name: Damaged wiring or loose connector at the solenoid

checks: Inspect the solenoid connector and wiring
Measure the solenoid resistance and compare to spec
Command the solenoid with a scan tool and check for a response
fix: Usually a new valve control solenoid or a wiring repair.

title: Intake Valve Control Solenoid Circuit (Bank 2)
plain: The intake valve control solenoid on bank 2 is an electric valve that adjusts valve timing or lift using oil pressure. The computer found a fault, such as an open circuit, in its circuit.

causes.name: Damaged wiring or loose connector at the solenoid

checks: Inspect the solenoid connector and wiring
Measure the solenoid resistance and compare to spec
Command the solenoid with a scan tool and check for a response
fix: Usually a new valve control solenoid or a wiring repair.

title: Fuel Rail/System Pressure - Too Low
plain: The computer measured fuel pressure in the fuel rail that is lower than it should be. The engine may not get enough fuel, especially when you accelerate hard or climb a hill.
symptoms: Loss of power or hesitation when accelerating
Engine may stall or go into limp mode

causes.name: Weak or failing fuel pump (in-tank or high-pressure pump)
Faulty fuel pressure regulator or volume regulator
Fuel leak, pinched line or very low fuel level

checks: Make sure there is enough fuel in the tank and replace the fuel filter if it is due
Check low-side fuel pressure with a gauge
Compare commanded and actual rail pressure with a scan tool
fix: On diesels a fuel filter often fixes it. Otherwise the usual fix is the fuel pump, the high-pressure pump on direct-injection engines, or a pressure regulator.
examples: Common on diesel pickups such as the GM Duramax and Ford Power Stroke when the fuel filter clogs or the high-pressure pump wears

title: Fuel Rail/System Pressure - Too High
plain: The computer measured fuel pressure in the fuel rail that is higher than it should be. This is most often seen on diesel and direct-injection engines.
symptoms: Possible limp mode or hard starting

causes.name: Stuck fuel pressure regulator or volume regulator
Wiring problem in the pressure control circuit

checks: Compare commanded and actual rail pressure with a scan tool
Inspect wiring to the rail pressure sensor and regulator
Check for a pinched or blocked return line
fix: Usually a new fuel pressure regulator or rail pressure sensor.

title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 1 Performance
plain: The fuel pressure regulator keeps fuel pressure at the right level. The computer saw that actual fuel pressure is not following what it commanded, so the regulator does not seem to be doing its job.

causes.name: Sticking or failed fuel pressure regulator
Contaminated fuel or clogged fuel filter

checks: Compare commanded and actual fuel pressure with a scan tool
Replace the fuel filter if it is due
Check low-side fuel supply pressure
fix: Often a new fuel pressure regulator, plus a fuel filter if it is due.

title: Low Pressure Fuel System Pressure - Too Low
plain: On engines with both a low-pressure and a high-pressure fuel pump, the computer measured that the low-pressure side (the in-tank pump supply) is lower than it should be.

causes.name: Faulty fuel pump control module or wiring

checks: Check low-side fuel pressure with a gauge
Check the fuel filter and pump wiring
fix: Usually a new in-tank fuel pump or fuel filter.

title: Low Pressure Fuel System Pressure - Too High
plain: On engines with both a low-pressure and a high-pressure fuel pump, the computer measured that the low-pressure side is higher than it should be.

causes.name: Blocked return line or stuck regulator

checks: Compare the low-side sensor reading against a mechanical gauge
Check the fuel pump control module and wiring
fix: Usually a new low-pressure fuel sensor or fuel pump control module.

title: Fuel Cooler Pump Control Circuit/Open
plain: Some diesels use a small electric pump to circulate coolant through a fuel cooler so fuel does not get too hot. The computer found an open or broken connection in the control circuit for this pump.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the vehicle drives
checks: Check the fuse and relay for the pump
Inspect the pump connector and wiring
fix: Usually a new fuel cooler pump or a wiring repair.

plain: Some diesels use a small electric pump to circulate coolant through a fuel cooler so fuel does not get too hot. The computer found a voltage that is too low in the control circuit for this pump.

fix: Usually a new fuel cooler pump or a wiring repair.

title: Engine Coolant Temperature/Fuel Temperature Correlation
plain: After the vehicle has sat long enough to cool down, the coolant temperature and fuel temperature readings should be close. The computer found they disagree by too much.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Block heater use before a cold start

checks: Compare the readings after the vehicle sits overnight
Ask whether a block heater was plugged in before the code set
fix: Usually replacing whichever sensor reads wrong.

title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 1 Control Circuit
plain: On many diesel and direct-injection engines, the fuel pressure regulator is electronically controlled. The computer found a fault, such as an open circuit, in the circuit that operates it.
symptoms: Hard starting, stalling or loss of power

causes.name: Damaged wiring or loose connector to the regulator

checks: Inspect the regulator connector and wiring
Measure the regulator resistance and compare to spec
fix: Usually a wiring repair or a new fuel pressure regulator.

title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 1 Control Circuit Low
plain: On many diesel and direct-injection engines, the fuel pressure regulator is electronically controlled. The computer found a voltage that is too low in the circuit that operates it.

causes.name: Damaged wiring or loose connector to the regulator

checks: Inspect the regulator connector and wiring

fix: Usually a wiring repair or a new fuel pressure regulator.

title: Fuel System Leak Detected - Large Leak
plain: The computer saw fuel pressure drop much faster than it should, and it believes there is a large fuel leak, usually on the high-pressure side of a diesel system.
symptoms: Engine may stall or refuse to restart
Fuel smell or visible fuel leak

causes.name: Leaking high-pressure fuel line or fitting
Leaking fuel filter housing or seals

checks: Look under the hood and under the vehicle for fuel leaks before driving
Inspect high-pressure lines, fittings and the filter housing
Have a shop check injector return flow
fix: Find and repair the leak. Diesel fuel on a hot engine or exhaust can catch fire, so do not keep driving with a visible leak.
examples: Well known on GM Duramax diesels, often from leaking fuel lines or injectors

title: Fuel System Leak Detected - Small Leak
plain: The computer saw fuel pressure drop a little faster than expected and suspects a small fuel leak in the fuel system.
checks: Look and smell for fuel leaks around the engine and under the vehicle
Inspect fuel lines, fittings and the filter housing
fix: Find and repair the leak, often a fitting, seal or injector.

title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit (Bank 1)
plain: Intake air temperature sensor 2 measures air temperature at a second point in the intake, often after the turbo or intercooler. The computer found a fault in the circuit from this sensor.
symptoms: Possible rough running or lower fuel economy
checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Compare its reading with other temperature sensors after a cold soak
fix: Usually a new intake air temperature sensor or a wiring repair.

title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1)
plain: Intake air temperature sensor 2 measures air temperature at a second point in the intake, often after the turbo or intercooler. The computer found a reading that does not make sense compared with other sensors from this sensor.
symptoms: Possible rough running or lower fuel economy

causes.name: Oil or dirt fouling the sensor

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Compare its reading with other temperature sensors after a cold soak
fix: Usually a new intake air temperature sensor or a wiring repair.

title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Low (Bank 1)
plain: Intake air temperature sensor 2 measures air temperature at a second point in the intake, often after the turbo or intercooler. The computer found a signal that is too low (often reads very hot) from this sensor.
symptoms: Possible rough running or lower fuel economy
checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Compare its reading with other temperature sensors after a cold soak
fix: Usually a new intake air temperature sensor or a wiring repair.

title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit High (Bank 1)

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
